root.summary: A worked runbook exemplar: what you'll see, the tags that classify severity/scope at a glance, a phase-strip you execute top to bottom, a legend so the colors mean something before you rely on them, and the table-list of exact commands. Copy this shape for any operational procedure someone follows under time pressure.

nodes.title: Cron job silently expired
nodes.tagline: Runbook — reference mode. Follow the phases top to bottom; don't skip the verify step.

blocks.text: A recurring cron job stopped firing and nobody was notified — here's how to confirm it, recover it, and prevent the next silent expiry.
blocks.sub: Session-only cron jobs auto-expire after 7 days with no notification. This is the recovery path, not a permanent fix.

items.label: Irreversible or high-blast-radius — read twice before running
Reversible but changes state — confirm the target first
Read-only — safe to run repeatedly while diagnosing

phases.name: Confirm
phases.desc: Is the job actually gone, or just quiet?

phases.name: Diagnose
phases.desc: Session-only expiry, or a real crash?

phases.name: Recover
phases.desc: Re-arm the job — this is the destructive step

phases.name: Verify
phases.desc: Confirm it actually fires before you walk away

blocks.lead: Phase 3 changes state — confirm the job name before running.
blocks.body: Re-arming with the wrong job name creates a second, orphaned job instead of fixing the original. There is no automatic dedup.

items.name: CronList()
items.note: Phase 1 — lists every active job for this session; the missing job confirms expiry, not crash

items.name: Check session age
items.note: Phase 2 — if the job's session has been alive 7+ days, this is the known auto-expiry, not a bug

items.name: CronCreate(same schedule, same prompt)
items.note: Phase 3 — re-arms the job under a NEW session-scoped id; the old id is gone for good

items.name: CronList() again, then wait one cycle
items.note: Phase 4 — confirm the new job appears AND actually fires once before considering this closed

blocks.label: Recovered
blocks.text: Recovery is complete only after phase 4's wait — a job that lists but never fires is still broken, and re-arming does not guarantee the underlying cause (session death, host restart) won't repeat it.

blocks.body: Session-only cron cannot be made durable from inside a session. If this job matters across restarts, it needs to move to a durably-scheduled mechanism outside this runbook's scope — file that as a follow-up, don't try to patch it here.
